scores.biggestWin: Give the header a subject. Right now the board is about a workflow; one 15px/600 ink line naming the nearest real event and its countdown — "Menu tasting · 1 Aug · in 14 days" — makes it about a wedding, and demoting the completion ratio and the overdue pill beneath it puts the loudest thing on screen where the meaning is. It is the only change in this set that converts competence into a moment.

Make the completion circle a real control. Ship `.tick` as a `<button role=\"checkbox\">` with its own hover, active, focus and keyboard binding, and take the darkening off `.card:hover` so the circle only responds when you are actually on it. Right now the board's central verb is a decorative span — no keyboard path, no honest pointer feedback — and every other interaction finding is downstream of the fact that the product's states were designed at card level and never at control level.

Unify the time chip to one grammar and one vocabulary. Every chip states the day the work is due — \"Mon 14 Jul\", \"Today\", \"Fri\", \"1 Aug\" — and lateness is carried entirely by the filled ink, with \"overdue\" as the only word for that state anywhere in the product. That single change makes the direction's own claim true (severity is fill, not a different sentence), removes the \"1 overdue\" versus \"2 days late\" collision, turns each tray into the column of dates the specimen sheet promises, and repairs four of the eight frames at once.

Give the couple its own typographic rank on the card and stop sharing one mono slot between clients and work areas. Right now the board answers "what status is everything in" but not "what is for Saturday's wedding", which is the only question a venue operator asks on the day — and the answer is buried in the faintest token on the card, spelled the same way as BAR and VENUE. Splitting client from area (ink-2 client first, ink-4 area behind a hairline) turns this from a competent generic kanban into something a venue can run a Saturday from, and it costs no colour, no weight and no change to the locked architecture. Separately and non-negotiably: the "5 of 32 done / DONE 9" contradiction in the dense frame is a blocker, not an improvement — no amount of design raises the score while the board contradicts itself on screen.

Add `text-wrap: balance` plus a hard `-webkit-line-clamp: 2` to `.cardTitle`. The card title is the only thing on this board a venue operator actually reads, it repeats 32 times in the dense frame, and right now it is set with no wrap control at a 22-character measure — producing one-word widows ("room", "list"), lines ending on "the" and "and", and three-line titles that break the tray's vertical rhythm and contradict the specimen sheet's own stated two-line contract. Two declarations fix the most-repeated element in the product in every frame at once.

Take the planning drawer out of overlay and put it in flow (`.sheet` becomes a row, `.drawer` becomes a static 388px column with an `inset 1px 0 0 var(--line)` left rule, `.board` switches to `grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: minmax(210px, 1fr)`). One change kills the worst frame in the set outright: no column is sliced at x=1034, no text truncates mid-word, the WAITING and DONE trays survive, the header stays visible above both panes, the drawer finally reads as an object rather than white-on-white, and the dock re-centres on the board it serves for free because its `left: 50%` now resolves against the board column instead of the whole sheet.

Make the planning drawer a real panel rather than an occlusion: inset the sheet by the drawer width (`.floor:has(.drawer) .sheet { margin-right: calc(388px + var(--inset)) }`) and give `.drawer` a declared edge (`box-shadow: var(--ring), 0 8px 40px rgba(17,17,17,0.10)`). It is roughly fifteen lines and it converts the one frame where the locked direction appears to break — a sentence sliced mid-word, two columns silently erased, white on white with no seam — into the deliberate two-surface moment the rest of the file already earns. Every other finding here is a correctness fix; this is the one that changes what the work looks like.

findings.element: .headFacts — the run "5 of 13 done · 1 overdue · day 11 of 97" in .head
findings.problem: The board has no subject. The one emotionally loaded fact this product owns — a real day approaching for real people — is set at 13px/400 in --ink-2, given identical visual weight to a completion ratio, and buried third in a grey run. "day 11 of 97" is season telemetry, not a reason to care. Meanwhile the loudest object on the entire screen is a filled-ink "1 overdue" pill that shouts and leads nowhere. A discerning stranger reads this header as workflow admin, not as a venue with a wedding coming. There is no memorable moment anywhere in the resting board, and this is where one was available for free.
findings.fix: Give the header a subject line. In head(), insert a new element immediately after .headRule and before .headFacts: Menu tasting · 1 Aug · in 14 days, sourced from the nearest dated task (the milestone if one exists, else the soonest due). Style it .headSubject { font-size:15px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-0.02em; color:var(--ink-1); white-space:nowrap; } — ink only, no indigo, so the accent is still spent once on the card. Then demote the rest: .headFacts { font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-3); } and drop its b { color:var(--ink-1) } override to color:var(--ink-2). Move .late to the end of .headFacts so the overdue pill no longer outranks the subject, and wrap it in a
findings.why: REFUTED. The CSS values quoted are accurate (floor.html:202-215), but the finding's central claims do not survive the frames or the code. (1) Factually wrong about the phone: at 390px the rule is hidden, .headName becomes width:100%/order:2 at 19px and .headActions takes order:1, so the wordmark sits alone on the top row with the action row between it and a full-width title — the clearest rank separation of any breakpoint, not "total failure". (2) It treats a logotype as a point on the UI type ramp. .word carries an indigo ::after dot; it is the product wordmark lockup, and lowercase logotypes are conventionally tracked tighter than the text ramp at exactly the named benchmarks. The rest of the file IS a clean monotone curve (18/-0.03, 14/-0.02, 13/-0.008, 12/-0.004, 10 caps/+0.04); the single exception is the mark, by design, not by oversight. (3) "Two co-equal titles with a 1px rule doing all the hierarchy work" is refuted at 2x zoom: lowercase tight mark + indigo dot left of the rule in the chrome zone, Title Case name with capitals and looser tracking right of it, with the fact row attached to the name. Rank is carried by case, accent, tracking and placement before size is asked to do anything. The fix would also make it worse — 15px/-0.02em strips the wordmark of its logotype setting and reads as a generic label, and 20px .headName compresses the step to the 22px [data-type="expressive"] variant at line 675.

findings.element: .board (padding 0 16px 96px) + .trayBody (overflow:auto; padding 2px 0 56px) + .dockScrim, in the dense frame
findings.problem: At 32 tasks the product fails at exactly the moment it should reassure. In locked-dense, the last card of four separate trays is dissolving into the dock's white scrim mid-word — "Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet", "Walk Aisling & Tom through the orchard on Sunday", "Gravel delivered for the top car park" are all half-erased under a floating pill. For a peak-season operator this reads as work disappearing. Underneath it is a structural fault: .trayBody sets overflow:auto while .board also sets overflow:auto, so each tray is a nested scroller inside the board scroller, the sticky .trayHead belongs to the wrong scroll context, and the 96px board padding never actually protects the inner scroller's content.
findings.why:
Verified against source and four frames; every factual claim holds.

CODE: `.cardTitle` (floor.html:345–349) is `font-size:14px; line-height:1.36; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-0.02em; color:var(--ink-1); margin:0; flex:1 1 auto; min-width:62%`. There is no `text-wrap`, no `hyphens`, no `-webkit-line-clamp`, no `overflow-wrap`. By contrast `.cardNote` (line 354) DOES carry `display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:2; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; overflow:hidden`. So the note is bounded and the title is not — the asymmetry is real and deliberate-looking but unhandled.

FRAMES: locked-dense confirms all three cited rags verbatim. WAITING column: "Waiting on Tom's guest / number before we hold the / room" — four-letter runt alone on line 3. REVIEW column: "Check the spring menu / against the new supplier / list" — same shape. IN PROGRESS: "Chase the florist / quote for the / spring date" — three lines for a 43-character title, with a violently uneven rag, because the `Friday` chip (`.when { flex:none }`) steals line 1. It is not confined to those three: DONE has "Open day, nine couples / through" and "Deposit invoice settled, Mara / & Finn" (an ampersand stranded on its own line), and REVIEW breaks on the hard hyphen in "recommended- / suppliers list". At tray width this is the dominant visual texture of the board.

SPEC CONTRADICTION: confirmed and the strongest part of the finding. floor.html:971 defines the LONG TITLE specimen with the caption "Two lines of title, then the note clamps. A card cannot run away." In locked-cards that specimen renders THREE title lines — "Confirm the marquee sides and / the wet-weather plan with the / hire company before Thursday" — and it renders them in a specimen cell WIDER than a real tray column, so in the tray it would be worse. The artifact states a contract in its own caption and the CSS does not implement it. Automation cannot see a caption disagreeing with the render; this is exactly what a human seat is for. Compounding it, `[data-density="compact"]` (line 639) tightens the note clamp to 1 line but leaves the title unbounded, so a compact card can still run 3 title lines — the density that is supposed to bound height bounds only the half that was already bounded.

Card height therefore becomes arbitrary across a tray, which is visible in locked-dense: the TO DO column's cards step 2/2/2 lines while IN PROGRESS steps 2/2/2/3/2, and the columns lose any shared rhythm.

SCOPE: typographic, no colour introduced, no layout restructured. In scope.

NOT REFUTED ON ANY GROUND — but the proposed CSS is over-reached in two specifics and I have sharpened it rather than accept it verbatim (see sharpenedFix). `overflow-wrap: anywhere` is wrong for natural-language venue-task titles: it permits unhyphenated mid-word breaks ("photog / rapher") and, unlike `break-word`, it shrinks the element's min-content contribution, which will fight `min-width: 62%` inside `.cardTitleRow`. And `text-wrap: balance` combined with `-webkit-line-clamp: 2` is self-defeating: balance distributes across the FULL untruncated line count first, so the 90-character LONG TITLE would balance to three short lines and then clamp to two under-filled ones with an ellipsis and a ragged right gutter — worse than two full lines plus an ellipsis. `pretty` is the correct tool here because it targets the last-line runt without shortening every line.

findings.element: locked-empty — the five .trayEmpty paragraphs and five .trayAdd buttons
findings.problem: A new operator's first screen is the least designed frame in the set: ten sentences of 12.5px --ink-3 prose spread across five columns, five identical grey ghost buttons, and not one element at full ink. There is no focal point, no primary action, no invitation — it reads as five apologies in a row. Emotionally it is a blank form. Compounding it, "Nothing held up" is the only empty line in the product without a full stop, while its four siblings all have one.
findings.fix: Delete 12.5px from floor.html entirely. Set .cardNote (352), .trayAdd (418), .drawerLine (493), .drawerTab (507), .drawerRow (524), .drawerAdd (542) and .loadSay (554) to 13px, and sweep the two the finding missed: [data-type="expressive"] .cardNote (678) and the mobile .headFacts (722) to 13px. Then give the empty board two distinct voices by size and density rather than by half a pixel: leave .trayNote at 12px/var(--ink-3) as the standing definition, and set .trayEmpty { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--ink-2); } as the live message. Resulting ramp: 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14 / 17 / 18 / 19. Do not claim a 15 or a 20 — collapsing 17/18/19 is a separate change with its own argument to make, and is not part of this fix.
findings.why: Verified in code and in frame. All ten cited declarations are exactly as stated (floor.html lines 303, 352, 360, 413, 418, 493, 507, 513, 524, 542, 554). The board renderer emits .trayNote and .trayEmpty together in every column, so locked-empty shows five pairs of consecutive ink-3 400-weight paragraphs separated only by 0.5px — the frame confirms they are visually one undifferentiated grey block, with no distinction between a permanent column definition and a transient call to act. That is a genuine hierarchy failure on the frame that most needs a voice, and it is invisible to the automated audit (palette, weight, contrast and hit targets all legitimately pass). The 2px/four-step cluster and the 14→17 hole are also accurate for the default state set. The fix is in scope: it introduces no hue, changes no layout, uses only the sanctioned ink-density mechanism, and improves contrast (ink-2 = 7.4:1 vs ink-3 = 5.3:1). Two defects in the fix as written, both correctable rather than disqualifying: it misses two further 12.5px declarations (line 678 expressive .cardNote, line 722 mobile .headFacts), and its stated "final ramp" of 10/11/12/13/14/15/20 is not what the edits produce — nothing in the fix creates a 15 or collapses 17/18/19 into 20.

findings.element: .head under @media (max-width: 720px) and .views overflow-x, in locked-board--390x844
findings.problem: The phone header wraps into an accident. flex-wrap plus order:1/2/3 leaves the "tasks." wordmark alone on the first line with roughly 60% of that line dead empty, the Share / Planning / more cluster floating below it and to the right against nothing, and the project name only arriving on a third band — about 480px of an 844px viewport spent before the first card. Directly beneath it the segmented view strip guillotines "Calendar" to "Calenda" at the sheet's edge with no fade, which reads as a bug rather than as scrollable content.
findings.fix: No change warranted. If a residual is ever pursued it is a copy question, not a type question: bare "High" is contextless English on a card ("high what?"). That would be a separate finding about the word, and it must not be answered by converting .hi to the mono label register — the sans/600 treatment is the card's own severity grammar (see .when overdue/today/milestone at floor.html:390-392) and is what keeps the priority separable from the couple tag at a glance.
findings.why: REFUTED. The CSS description is accurate (.hi is sans/12px/sentence-case/600 against .tag's mono/11px/uppercase/400), but the argument built on it fails on three counts. (1) The load-bearing claim is false in the frames: titles are 15px/600 at --ink-1 and "High" is 12px/600 at --ink-2 sitting beneath them, so in locked-dense, locked-board and the 390px frame the title wins every card. There is no hierarchy inversion and no "bold speckle that the eye catches before the titles". The count is also wrong — data.js carries 4 priority:"High" in BOARD plus 2 in DENSE_EXTRA, so six cards in dense, not eight. (2) The rule comment at line 290 sits directly above .trayName and governs the mono label class; the card footer is already, by design, one mono label followed by sans facts — .cm (comment count) is sans 12px 400 on the same line. .hi is consistent with the local system, not an outlier introducing a register clash. Further, .when (lines 390-392) sets font-weight 600 for overdue, today and milestone: weight 600 IS this card's severity marker, the non-hue expression of urgency the direction demands. .hi at 600/--ink-2 speaks that established grammar. (3) The fix makes it worse. Two adjacent uppercase mono tracked tokens separated only by an --ink-3/--ink-2 alpha step at 11px is a near-invisible distinction; "MARA & FINN HIGH" would scan as two tags, destroying the instant label-vs-value read on the one footer fact that drives triage, and demoting the more actionable datum (priority) beneath the less actionable one (which couple). It also leaves .cm in sans, so the footer becomes mono + mono + sans — a stranger mix than today's deliberate mono-label-then-sans-facts.

findings.element: The WAITING tray in locked-board--1440x960 (the flagship frame)
findings.problem: The hero shot of a locked direction ships with a dead column: WAITING shows count 0, an empty-state sentence, and a lone ghost button, punching a full-height white hole through the right-centre of the sheet while its four siblings carry work. A stranger's first read of the flagship frame is that one fifth of the board does nothing. The dense frame proves the column works, which makes its emptiness in the default fixture a self-inflicted wound.
findings.why: CONFIRMED, with the fix corrected. The diagnosis is factually right: EMPTY_COPY (floor.html:873-879) gives todo/doing/done messages that wrap to two lines at 1440 tray width, while review and Waiting's c.empty are one line, and locked-empty--1440x960.png shows the five Add task rows split across two baselines (~18px apart, not 19.5 — one line box of 12.5px x 1.45 = 18.125px). The cause is structural, not incidental: .trayAdd is a sibling AFTER .trayBody (line 896) and .trayBody has no flex-grow, so the button's y is a pure function of the paragraph's line count. Nothing pins it. In the populated board this rag is correct — the action follows the content. In the empty state there is no content, so the stagger is driven only by sentence length, on the one frame where composition is the entire product. The file's own stated principle ("One optical baseline", line 307) argues for locking it. Not already handled, not a palette or architecture change, in scope. HOWEVER the proposed value is wrong: foundation.css:101-104 sets box-sizing: border-box globally and .trayEmpty carries padding: 8px 4px 4px, so min-height: 37px sizes the BORDER box — a one-line tray goes 30.1px to 37px while a two-line tray stays at 48.25px, halving the rag to 11px instead of removing it. The magic pixel also silently breaks if the 12.5px size or 1.45 line-height ever moves.

findings.element: `.tick` inside `.card` — floor.html card() renders `<span class="tick">`; CSS at .tick / `.card:hover .tick`
findings.problem: The board's single most-used action, completing a task, is not a control. It is a span: not focusable, no role, no aria state, no keyboard path, no :active. Its only feedback (`box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.4px var(--ink-2)`) fires on hover of the whole card, so the circle looks armed while the cursor is 300px away on the title, and looks identical whether the pointer is on it or not. The one thing the card exists to do has no state of its own, and a keyboard user cannot tick anything off — only the wrapping `<article tabindex="0">` takes focus, and Enter on it is bound to nothing.
findings.fix:
Move `.drawer` into `.sheet` in the DOM (it is currently a sibling at line 992 — `floor > rail + sheet + drawer`) and take it out of overlay:

1. Wrap `.head`, `.views`, `.board` in `.main { flex:1; min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; position:relative }`; set `.sheet { flex-direction: row }`.
2. `.drawer { position:static; flex:none; width:388px; border-radius:0; box-shadow: inset 1px 0 0 var(--line) }` — drop right/top/bottom/z-index. `.sheet` already has `overflow:hidden` + `border-radius:var(--r-sheet)`, so the sheet's own top-right/bottom-right corners still clip correctly; `border-radius:0` on the drawer is right.
3. `.board { grid-template-columns:none; grid-auto-flow:column; grid-auto-columns:minmax(210px,1fr); overflow-x:auto }`. At 1440 with no drawer this yields 5x257.2 — pixel-identical to today. With the drawer open the board track is 898px, so the five trays scroll rather than being sliced, and DONE stays reachable.

Two things the original proposal misses and that will break other states if left:

4. **`.dockScrim` must move into `.main` too.** It is `position:absolute; left:0; right:0` inside `.sheet` (line 425). Left where it is, the white fade gradient stretches under the drawer and paints a soft horizontal band across the drawer's own footer. Move it with the dock so both resolve against `.main`.

5. **The responsive overrides for `.drawer` become dead or wrong.** `@media (max-width:900px) { .drawer { left:var(--inset); width:auto } }` (line 692) and `@media (max-width:720px) { .drawer { top:60px; bottom:calc(60px + var(--inset)*2) } }` (line 729) are all overlay-only properties that no longer apply to a static element. Replace with: at =900px, `.sheet { flex-direction:column }` and `.drawer { width:auto; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--line) }` so the drawer becomes a bottom sheet inside the same white surface, or restore it as a deliberate full-width overlay with a scrim — but it must be re-specified, not inherited.

While in there: give the drawer's Close a paired state on the header's Planning button (`[data-active]`), since with the fix that button now stays visible and should read as the open toggle.
findings.why: Confirmed on every measurable claim. `.drawer` (floor.html:477-485) is `position:absolute; right/top/bottom:var(--inset); width:388px; background:var(--white)` with no border, no box-shadow and no rule, and it is a DOM sibling of `.sheet` (line 992), not a child — so it is a second white slab floating over an identical white one. A pixel scan of locked-planning down x=1027-1042 CSS finds 88 of 90 sampled rows pure white (the 2 exceptions are glyphs), while the real `.tray` rule at x=890 renders at (241,241,241): the drawer has no visible edge. Geometry checks out: sheet spans 104-1422, `.board` is `repeat(5, minmax(0,1fr))` inside `padding:0 16px`, so tracks are 257.2px and WAITING occupies 891.6-1148.8 with DONE at 1148.8-1406. The drawer's left edge at 1034 cuts WAITING in half and buries DONE entirely — and because `.board` is a fixed 5x1fr grid at this width it cannot scroll, so DONE is unreachable, not offscreen. `.trayNote` has no line-clamp and no text-overflow, so "Held by a reply, a delive" is a hard overlay clip with no ellipsis, and `.trayCount` (emitted at line 890) is hidden under the panel. The header loss is worse than the finding states: comparing locked-board to locked-planning, the drawer erases `.viewTools` (Filter/Sort/Display) as well as `.headActions` (Share/Planning 5/...), so the Planning control disappears the instant it is used — no active state, no visible way back. Dock: `left:50%` resolves against `.sheet` at 763 while the visible region 104-1034 centres on 569; measured from the frame the dock spans 574-948, leaving 470px of air left and 86px right. Not out of scope: no hue is added, type is untouched, and none of the five locked elements change — putting the drawer in flow inside the sheet actually restores "one white sheet" rather than breaking it.

findings.element: `.cardDots` (`opacity: 0` → `opacity: 1` only under `.card:hover`), plus the `@media (pointer: coarse)` block that sizes it to 44×44
findings.problem: Two failures in one control. On desktop, `.cardDots` is a real `<button>` inside a focusable card with no `:focus-visible` reveal rule, so tabbing into a card puts focus on a fully invisible button — the focus ring paints on nothing. On touch, where hover never fires, the coarse-pointer rule inflates that invisible button to a 44×44 target pinned at `top: 2px; right: 2px` with pointer events live: on the tablet and phone frames every card has an invisible 44px tap trap over its top-right corner that swallows taps meant for the title, and the menu it belongs to can never be revealed at all. There is no touch path to per-task actions anywhere in the product.
findings.fix:
Move the dock clearance from the grid onto the tray box, leaving the tray body untouched.

1. `.board { padding: 0 16px; }` — drop the 96px.
2. `.tray { padding: 14px 12px 104px; }` — was `14px 12px 8px`. 104 = the 96px that left the board plus the 8px the tray already had, so the scrolling box in the dense state keeps exactly the height it has today. Because `border-left` is painted on the tray's border box, the rule now runs the tray's full stretched height and resolves on the sheet's foot instead of in mid-air.
3. Leave `.trayBody { padding: 2px 0 56px; }` alone. Its bottom padding is the gap between the last card and the tray's own "Add task" button; inflating it to 132px pushes that button down 76px in every column and breaks its relationship to the stack.
4. Reset where the dock is absent: add `padding-bottom: 8px;` to `.tray` inside the `@media (max-width: 720px)` block (`.dock, .dockScrim { display: none }` there, so 104px would be dead space above the phone sheet foot), and change `[data-density="compact"] .tray { padding: 12px 9px 6px }` to `12px 9px 102px` — that rule resets padding wholesale, so without it compact would run cards under the dock.

Resolution at the foot: the full-width `.dockScrim` (108px, transparent to solid white) will now fade the last 108px of each rule out before the edge. That is already a graceful termination rather than a cut. If the companion dock-local-scrim change lands, the two outer rules land hard on the sheet's bottom edge and only the centre pair softens under the dock, which is the stronger reading — but this fix stands on its own without it.
findings.why: CONFIRMED on measurement, with the fix corrected. Source: `.board { padding: 0 16px 96px }` carries the dock clearance on the grid, so the stretched `.tray` row — and with it every `border-left` — ends 96px above the sheet foot. Pixel scan of the four tray boundaries (x=374/632/890/1148 CSS) confirms all rules terminate at y=845.5 against a sheet foot of 942 in locked-empty, locked-board and locked-loading, and at ~856 in locked-dense. Dock top is 876, so the cut lands 30px above it, and the dock spans only x 571-950, leaving the 374 and 1148 rules ending over nothing at all. The dockScrim is only ~24% opaque at that y (tail pixel 244 against the rule's own 241), so these are hard stops, not fades. In the empty and loading frames the four hairlines are the entire structure on screen and they quit in mid-air on an invisible horizontal that corresponds to nothing. That is a real, specific, visible failure of the direction's one structural claim, and it is not something the automated audit can see. The proposed fix as written, however, would regress: `.trayBody` is not `flex: 1`, it hugs content, and `.trayAdd` is its next sibling, so `.trayBody`'s bottom padding is the visible gap between the last card and that column's Add-task button (measured ~80-105px in board and empty). Taking it from 56px to 132px would drop every Add-task button a further 76px and detach it from its stack. The clearance must move to the tray box, not the tray body.

findings.element: `.tray` (`transition: background-color …` with no rule that ever changes it) and the "In flight" specimen on locked-cards
findings.problem: Drag is the board's defining gesture and only the half in your hand is designed. The card in flight gets a rotate, a scale and the one heavy shadow — and the destination gets nothing: no tray tint, no insertion gap, no rule where the card will land, no state for the tray you are leaving. The `.tray` background transition is vestigial, wired to no selector. In the dense frame, dragging a card into a 10-card TO DO tray gives the operator no idea what row it lands on until they let go. The specimen sheet calls itself "every card state" while the state that needs the most design is missing from the board.
findings.fix:
Delete `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;` from the `body` block (floor.html line 108 — keep `font-feature-settings: "ss01", "cv01"` on the line above). Then re-declare it only where digits genuinely stack or tick in a fixed slot: `.trayCount`, `.when`, `.cardFoot .cm`, `.ghost em`, `.drawerTab em`, `.axisEnds`, `.drawerSummary`. Group them as one rule with a comment naming the reason, so the intent survives the next edit: `/* Tabular is for digits that stack in a column or tick in place. Prose keeps Geist's proportional figures. */`.

Go one step further than the finding on two of its items. `.headFacts` ("5 of 13 done", "day 11 of 97") and `.late` ("1 overdue") are single-line sentences with nothing aligned above or below them — they are read, not scanned as a column, and the crop shows "13" and "11" splitting apart exactly as the card titles do. Give those proportional figures too; the sub-pixel reflow when 5 becomes 6 is imperceptible and the row is left-anchored. Consider dropping `.drawerLine` ("Wedding season · 6 Jul – 10 Oct") from the tabular list for the same reason, unless you want it locked to the `.axisEnds` beneath it — that one is a legitimate judgement call.

`.when` must stay tabular regardless: the specimen sheet's own copy claims "the time fact right-aligns on the title's own line so a tray reads as a column of dates", and that promise depends on it.
findings.why: CONFIRMED. The defect is real, measurable in the shipped font binary, and visible in the frames. fontTools on the actual vendored fonts/Geist.woff2 shows Geist's default figures are proportional (one = 384/1000, zero = 663, seven = 524) and that the font carries a real tnum lookup substituting every digit for a .tf variant at a flat 600 units. So the body rule adds 216 units — 0.216em — of sidebearing to every "1"; at 14px .cardTitle that is +3.0px per digit, and 6px of dead space inside "11am". Visually confirmed by crops of locked-board: "Clear Sunday 11am late checkout" reads as "1 1am" with both ones adrift in empty slots, "June 2027" is conspicuously airier than "June" and "walk-in" around it, and the header's "13", "day 11 of 97" and "1 overdue" show the same gap. The decisive point is an internal contradiction in the sheet's own type: .cardTitle sets letter-spacing: -0.02em — the designer explicitly tightening titles — while inheriting 0.216em of loose slot on every 1. The tabular rule is spending ten times more space than the tracking claws back, in the same string. That is a defect, not taste. The fix is safe and complete: GeistMono.woff2 has no tnum feature and is fixed-width (all digits 600), so every mono micro-label is unaffected by removing the body rule; the re-declaration list covers every genuinely ticking or aligning element, and correctly omits .drawerRow, which carries the same "June 2027" prose title. It introduces no hue, changes no layout, adds no weight. Two minor inaccuracies do not undermine it: "Two extra cases of tonic" contains no digit (mis-cited example), and "1 Aug" sits in .when, which the finding's own fix keeps tabular, so it should not have been cited as a symptom. Note the line number is 108, not 104.

findings.element: `.dockScrim` (108px white gradient, full sheet width) + `.dock` over the trays, seen in locked-dense
findings.problem: In peak season the dock does not float above empty floor, it sits on top of live work. In the dense frame the last card of TO DO ("Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet"), of IN PROGRESS ("Walk Aisling & Tom through the orchard on Sunday") and of DONE ("Gravel delivered for the top car park") are all faded to near-illegible by the scrim, and the dock body covers the middle of that band outright. Because the scrim is `pointer-events: none`, those cards stay clickable while being unreadable — the worst pairing: you can hit a task you cannot read. `.trayBody`'s `padding-bottom: 56px` is less than half the 108px scrim, so the reserve was set to the wrong number.
findings.fix: Nothing structural. The only defensible residue is the gradient ramp, not its scope: `0.90 at 42%` reaches near-opacity high enough that a card title reads half-legible rather than cleanly gone. If the panel wants it, soften to `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0), rgba(255,255,255,0.86) 52%, var(--white) 100%)` and leave `left: 0; right: 0; height: 108px` exactly as shipped. That is taste, not a defect.
findings.why:
Factually wrong on its load-bearing claim, and the fix would make the composition worse.

(1) The trap claim is false. The finding compares the 108px scrim against `.board { padding-bottom: 96px }` only, ignoring three other boxes in the stack: `.trayBody { padding: 2px 0 56px }`, `.trayAdd` (36px + 4px margin), and `.tray { padding: 14px 12px 8px }`. Real clearance below the last card is 96+8+44+56 = 204px. Measured in headless Chromium at 1440x960, state=dense, scrolled to the end: the last card in To Do (10 cards, the tallest tray) sits 200px above the sheet bottom and 92px above the scrim's top edge — fully clear. In Progress 356px clear, Done 322px clear. "Can never be seen clean" is false in every column.

(2) The scope claim misreads what the scrim serves. Measured, `.board` is the single scroll container (scrollHeight 1333 vs clientHeight 811); no `.trayBody` scrolls independently. The fade therefore belongs to the board, which is full-bleed, not to the 373px dock. A full-width bottom fade on a full-width scrolling region is correctly scoped. In locked-board (13 tasks, no overflow) the scrim sits over empty white and is invisible — it only appears when a "more below" cue is wanted. The fogged titles the finding names are the resting scroll position of a scrollable board, not damage.

(3) The fix is a regression. A 720px centred radial would leave columns 1 and 5 hard-clipping against the sheet's bottom radius while columns 2-4 fade — an asymmetric edge on a surface whose premise is one continuous white sheet. Its `--white 34%` core is heavier behind the dock than the current linear at the same heights, so the middle columns get more fog, not less, and the horizontal falloff cuts a visible lens across the vertical tray rules. The 132px trayBody padding is redundant against 204px of existing clearance and adds dead scroll to short trays.

findings.element: `.dockField` and `.dockPrimary` at 768×1024 (locked-board--768x1024)
findings.problem: The dock breaks at tablet. "Search this project" wraps onto two lines inside the pill and "Add task" wraps onto two lines inside the primary button, so both dock controls render as squashed two-line blocks with the ⌘K chip stranded beside them. Neither element sets `white-space: nowrap`, and `.dockField`'s `min-width: 196px` fights the shrunk sheet. This is the product's primary entry point for both search and creation and it is visibly broken on the one size a venue operator is most likely to use behind a desk.
findings.fix: Fix the cause, not just the symptom. The dock wraps because it is absolutely positioned at left:50% with no right and no width, which caps its shrink-to-fit width at half the sheet. On .dock add `width: max-content; max-width: calc(100% - var(--inset) * 2);` so the pill takes its natural width at every size and only ever clamps to the sheet. Add `white-space: nowrap` to .dockField and .dockPrimary as insurance so a longer project label can never re-introduce the wrap. Then, inside the existing `@media (max-width: 900px)` block, reduce `.dockField { min-width: 148px; }` so the field yields before the sheet does. Do NOT hide the kbd chip by width — hide it inside the existing `@media (pointer: coarse)` block (`.dockField kbd { display: none; }`), which is the only accurate test for "there is no ⌘ here" and correctly leaves it visible in a narrow laptop window. Drop the "below 720px collapse to the icon" clause entirely: the dock is already `display: none` there and search/add are already re-homed to .headSearch and .railAdd. Re-shoot locked-board--768x1024 and confirm both labels sit on one line and the pill is horizontally centred within the sheet.
findings.why: Confirmed in both the frame and the code. locked-board--768x1024.png shows "Search this / project" and "Add / task" each broken onto two lines with the kbd chip stranded beside the wrapped label; the same dock at 1440 (locked-board, locked-planning) is one clean line, so it is a genuine tablet-only break, not an intended state. In floor.html, .dockField (L441) and .dockPrimary (L458) set no white-space (grep shows nowrap used at L214/220/239/386/400 but never on the dock), .dockField carries min-width:196px (L444), and no media query touches the dock between 900px and the 720px breakpoint where it is hidden outright (L728). The actual mechanism is stronger than the finding states: .dock is position:absolute with left:50%, no right and no width (L431), so its shrink-to-fit width is capped at containing-block minus left, i.e. half the sheet, about 372px at 768 versus a ~380px max-content dock. Nothing else handles this, no non-negotiable is touched (no colour, no weight, no layout restructure), and the dock is the primary search and create entry point on the size a venue operator most plausibly uses. Two clauses of the proposed fix are wrong and are corrected in the sharpened version: the sub-720px icon-collapse is already handled (dock hidden, search in .headSearch and add in .railAdd, visible in locked-board--390x844.png), and hiding the kbd by viewport width would wrongly hide it on a narrow laptop window and wrongly show it as absent on an iPad with a hardware keyboard, so the existing @media (pointer: coarse) block (L572) is the correct gate.

findings.element: Card time chip — floor.html `timeOf()` line 656–658, rendered as "2 days late" / "Today" / "Friday" / "1 Aug"; and the header pill `.late` reading "1 overdue"
findings.problem: One board scan carries four grammars for one fact: an elapsed duration ("2 days late"), a deictic ("Today"), a weekday ("Friday") and an absolute date ("1 Aug"). Worse, the same state has two names in the same frame — the header says "1 overdue", the card says "2 days late". The specimen sheet's own thesis is that severity is expressed by ink density and fill, never by hue, but the copy breaks that thesis by ALSO changing the sentence when severity changes. And the overdue string is hardcoded, not derived: line 656 returns the literal "2 days late" regardless of the task's `due` value ("Overdue by 2 days"), so the data model and the chip disagree.
findings.fix:
Make the tick a real control and give it the two-rung ladder every other control in the file already has.

1. Markup (line 807): `'<button type="button" class="tick" role="checkbox" aria-checked="' + (done ? "true" : "false") + '" aria-label="' + (done ? "Mark not done: " : "Mark done: ") + esc(task.title) + '">' + I.check + "</button>"`. Reset UA button styles on `.tick` (`border:0; padding:0; background:none; font:inherit; -webkit-appearance:none`) so the 18px circle is unchanged pixel-for-pixel.

2. Demote card hover, promote tick hover. Replace line 342 with two rules:
   `.card:hover .tick, .card[data-force="hover"] .tick { background: var(--wash); }`  (rest-state hint only)
   `.tick:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.4px var(--ink-2); background: var(--wash-2); }`  (the ring now means "you are on it")

3. Press: `.tick:active { transform: scale(0.92); }` using the existing `--dur`/`--curve` tokens in the transition already declared on `.tick` — add `transform` to that transition list rather than a raw duration.

4. Focus ring: the global rule at line 112 already covers `button:focus-visible`, but it forces `border-radius: var(--r-chip)`, which would draw a rounded rectangle around a circle. Add only `.tick:focus-visible { border-radius: 50%; }` — do not restate outline or colour.

5. Done state: `.card[data-done] .tick` zeroes the shadow (407), so un-ticking currently has no affordance. Add `.card[data-done] .tick:hover { background: var(--ink-1); }` — ink density, no new hue.

6. Touch targets: add `.tick` to the `@media (pointer: coarse)` rule at 573, but grow the hit area without growing the mark — `.tick { position: relative; } .tick::after { content:""; position:absolute; inset:-13px; }` under the coarse query, so the visible circle stays 18px and the target reaches 44px. This is the gap the automated hit-target pass could not see, because a span was never measured.

7. Drop the Space-on-card binding from the original proposal. A real button is a tab stop and answers Enter natively; with `role="checkbox"` bind Space on the tick itself to toggle. Do not bind Space on `.card` — it is the page-scroll key for keyboard users and would put the card and its tick in contention. If a second tab stop per card is judged too costly at 32-card density, the correct alternative is `tabindex="-1"` on the tick plus a single-letter shortcut on the focused card (Linear's pattern), never Space.
findings.why: Confirmed against source and four frames. Line 807 renders the tick as `<span class="tick">` while the sibling overflow control on line 816 is a real `<button aria-label="Task actions">` — the file's own convention marks controls as buttons, and the single most-used action was left as text with no role, no aria-checked, no focus stop. Its only pointer feedback is `.card:hover .tick` (line 342); there is no `.tick:hover`, `:active`, or `:focus-visible`, so the ring darkens when the cursor is anywhere on the card and reads identically whether the pointer is on the circle or not. The HOVER specimen in locked-cards shows exactly this. Contrast `.cardDots`, which gets both a card-hover reveal (375) and its own `.cardDots:hover` (376) — the two-rung ladder the tick was denied. Two further consequences the finding did not name but which follow from the same defect: the `@media (pointer: coarse)` rule (573) enlarges `.cardDots, .ghost, .trayAdd, .drawerTab, .drawerRow button, .drawerAdd, .drawerHelp a` to 44px and omits `.tick`, so on the 390px frame the primary action is an 18px circle (16px compact, line 647) while the secondary menu is 44px — the hit-target audit passed it only because a span is not a control; and `.card[data-done] .tick` sets `box-shadow: none` (407), leaving un-ticking with no affordance at all. Not a taste claim, not handled elsewhere, and it breaks no locked constraint: no colour, type weight, or architecture change is involved. The proposed fix is right in shape but wrong in two specifics — binding Space on the focused card steals page scroll from keyboard users and puts the card and tick in contention for one key, and a bare `.tick:focus-visible` outline inherits `border-radius: var(--r-chip)` from the global rule at line 112, drawing a rounded rectangle around a circle. Sharpened accordingly.

findings.element: Empty board frame (locked-empty) — header `.headFacts` "0 of 0 done", and the five `EMPTY_COPY` lines in floor.html:744–750
findings.problem: Two defects on the product's most-scrutinised first-run surface. First, "0 of 0 done" is a dead string: it states nothing and reads like broken data on a board that has never been used. Second, the five column lines open with the same word five times in a horizontal row — "Nothing agreed yet…", "Nothing in motion…", "Nothing waiting on a check.", "Nothing held up", "Nothing finished yet…". Read left to right that is a template, not writing, and it is the one frame where the reader has nothing else to look at. "Nothing held up" also drops the full stop the other four carry (data.js `empty:` override), so the row is not even internally consistent.
findings.fix: Derive every header fact from the rendered set, and only that. In `head()` replace the `total`/`done`/chip lines with: `const lanes = B.columns.map(c => tasksFor(c.id)); const all = lanes.flat(); const total = all.length; const done = tasksFor("done").length; const overdue = all.filter(t => timeOf(t).kind === "overdue").length; const undated = all.filter(t => timeOf(t).kind === "none").length;` then render `overdue` in the late chip and `undated` in the Planning chip in place of `p.overdue` and `p.undated` — the Planning chip is hardcoded the same way and reads 5 against 19 undated tasks in the dense frame. `p.day`/`p.of` stay fixture facts, correctly. This makes the empty state fall out of the same expression (0 of 0, no chips) and deletes the `state === "empty"` and `state === "dense"` special cases from `head()` entirely, so no future state can desync. Do NOT hide the DONE tray numeral: the five tray counts are one ruled row and removing one breaks the system to fix a duplication that is not one.
findings.why: Confirmed against source and frames. floor.html:840-841 recomputes `total` for the dense state but leaves `done` bound to the fixture (`p.done = 5`, data.js:22). Counting the fixture gives dense lanes {todo:10, doing:7, review:4, waiting:2, done:9} = 32, and locked-dense--1440x960.png shows the header reading "5 of 32 done" while the DONE tray head reads 9, both above the fold on the same screen. locked-board--1440x960.png is consistent (5 of 13, tray 5), so the contradiction appears only in the peak-season frame that state exists to prove. The finding understates the problem: `p.undated = 5` is hardcoded the same way, so the dense header also reads "Planning 5" against 19 actually-undated tasks. Two of four header facts are wrong in that frame. The diagnosis and the derive-from-the-rendered-set half of the fix are correct. The second half of the proposed fix is refused: hiding the DONE tray numeral breaks a five-across system rule to solve a duplication that is not one, since a header fraction and a per-lane count are different altitudes of the same object, and every benchmark board shows both.

findings.element: Card foot — the priority token, rendered as a bare bold "High" beside the uppercase tag (`<span class="hi">` in `card()`)
findings.problem: "MARA & FINN  High" is a sentence fragment with no subject. This product is for wedding-venue operators, not software teams, and the repo's own north star ranks utility with a first-contact test: a surface that needs explaining is not done. "High" is project-management jargon shorthand that only reads correctly to someone who already knows a task board has a priority field. It also competes typographically with the title because it is the only other weight-600 string on the card.
findings.fix:
Design the destination, not just the hand. Four rules, in the same ink-only language.

1. Drop target. `.tray[data-over] { background: var(--wash); }` — and you must carry it through the sticky head, or the tinted column gets a white band across its top: `.trayHead` is `position: sticky` with `background: var(--white)` (floor.html:284-288) and needs to stay opaque to occlude scrolling cards. Composite the same two tokens instead of inventing a hex: `.tray[data-over] .trayHead { background: linear-gradient(var(--wash), var(--wash)), var(--white); }`.

2. Insertion marker inside `.trayBody` at the computed index: `.dropLine { height: 2px; border-radius: 1px; background: var(--ink-1); }` — no margin needed, the tray's existing `gap: 8px` already spaces it. Note this breaks the file's own stated law at lines 47-49 ("Nothing on a white surface goes above 8%: a heavier rule reads as a box"). Do not silently break it and do not water the line down to `--line-strong`, which reads as a shadow at the exact moment the operator needs certainty. Follow the convention the file already uses for the tooltip duration: write the exception down in the ladder comment — "full ink at 2px exists once, for the drop line, because a landing position is the one rule that may not be misread."

3. Source vacated. `opacity: 0` does not close the row, it holds the space open — which is the opposite of what your own fix note asks for. Remove the source card from flow on pickup and let the `gap: 8px` in `.trayBody` close over it within `--dur`. Drop the `.card[data-force="drag"] { opacity: 1 }` clause entirely; it is a no-op against the default.

4. Delete or wire the dead declaration. Once `[data-over]` exists the line 280 transition is earning its place; if the drop model is deferred again, the transition goes with it. A locked sheet should not ship a rule pointed at nothing.

Then add three specimens to the card sheet — "drop target", "insertion", "source vacated". Row three of the sheet currently runs LONG TITLE and IN FLIGHT with two cells empty, so two of the three cost no new row.
findings.why: Verified in source. `.tray` (floor.html:275-281) carries `transition: background-color var(--dur) var(--curve)` and every other `.tray` selector in the file (282, 291, 292, 642, 726) is a border reset, a `.pip` descendant, a compact padding override, or mobile scroll-snap — no rule sets a tray background in any state, so the transition is genuinely dead. The only drag design that exists is `.card[data-force="drag"]` (327-330: rotate, scale, `--lift`); there is no `[data-over]`, no insertion element and no ghost/source state anywhere in 1012 lines. The dense frame confirms the cost: TO DO holds 10 cards in a scrolling tray, so a drop lands at an unknowable index. The finding is not a taste claim and not out of scope — the product's own brief already declares the intent it is missing (DIRECTIONS.md:170, "the destination tray deepens under the pointer"), which is precisely what the vestigial transition was written for and then abandoned. Tokens for the fix already exist (`--wash`, `--ink-1`), the tray stays a ruled column with a transient tint rather than a filled box, and nothing here adds a hue or moves the architecture. Two small overstatements do not sink it: the missing drop-target tint is a tray state rather than a card state, so "every card state" is not literally falsified — but the source-vacated ghost IS a card state and is genuinely absent from the sheet. The proposed fix itself is technically wrong in four places and is corrected below.

findings.element: Indigo spend across the planning frame — milestone chip, focus/selection ring, wordmark dot, rail active dot, drawer axis playhead, and the "Select all" text link
findings.problem: The specimen sheet prints the claim "The one earned indigo in the whole view" under the milestone card. On the planning frame that claim is false four times over: indigo appears on the axis playhead and on a "Select all" utility link, which is the least consequential control on the surface. Spending the single accent on a bulk-select convenience devalues it everywhere else — once indigo means "select all", it stops meaning "this is the next milestone". The palette is obeyed but not spent.
findings.fix:
Three edits, in priority order.

1. Kill the phantom target at the rule that creates it, not per-breakpoint. At L371 make the hidden state inert, and pair every reveal with pointer-events:
   `.cardDots { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }`
   `.card:hover .cardDots, .card[data-force="hover"] .cardDots, .card:focus-within .cardDots, .cardDots:focus-visible { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; }`
   This single change removes the tap trap on both touch frames even if nothing else lands, and it makes the keyboard ring paint on something. Adopt it as a house rule: no `pointer-events`-live control may sit at `opacity: 0`.

2. Give touch a real, permanent affordance in the coarse block, since `:focus-within` does nothing for a finger:
   `@media (pointer: coarse) { .cardDots { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; background: transparent; color: var(--ink-4); } }`
   Ink-4 on white keeps it the quietest mark on the card, so a phone board does not read as 32 menu buttons.

3. Stop the corner collision structurally rather than only at touch. The 28px desktop box already overlaps the right end of an overdue or due-today chip on hover — the HOVER specimen only escapes it because that card carries no `when` chip. Reserve the corner in `.cardTitleRow` at both sizes (`padding-right: 30px`, and `44px` inside the coarse block) so the chip's right edge sits at one uniform inset on every card. The "tray reads as a column of dates" intent survives because the inset is identical across cards; what dies is the white 28px box landing on top of an overdue chip.

If the locked direction is instead that per-task actions on touch come from opening the task, then delete `.cardDots` on coarse pointers outright (`display: none`) and ship the task sheet — but no such sheet exists anywhere in floor.html today, so edits 1–3 are the shippable answer.
findings.why: Confirmed on both halves, verified in source and frames. (1) `.cardDots` (floor.html L371) is `opacity: 0`, revealed only by `.card:hover` (L375), yet it is emitted as a real `<button>` (L816) inside `<article class="card" tabindex="0">`. Grep for focus selectors returns only L112 (global ring) and L322 (`.card:focus-visible`) — there is no focus reveal for the button. Since opacity applies to an element's outline too, tabbing past the card lands on a tab stop whose indigo focus ring renders at zero alpha: the keyboard user's focus disappears mid-card. The KEYBOARD FOCUS specimen in locked-cards shows the ring on the card with no menu present, documenting the gap rather than covering it. (2) The `@media (pointer: coarse)` block (L572–577) sizes that still-invisible button to 44×44 at `top: 2px; right: 2px`, and `pointer-events` is never touched anywhere on it (the file's only `pointer-events: none` is L429, the dock scrim). No max-width block hides it. So on the 768 and 390 frames every card carries a live invisible 44×44 target over its top-right corner, sitting over the end of the first title line and the right end of the `.when` chip — and since hover never fires on touch, the menu it belongs to is unreachable by intent and only reachable by accident. Grep confirms `.cardDots` is the only `opacity: 0` control in the file, so this is a single specific defect, not a pattern complaint. It survives every refutation test: not factually wrong; not handled elsewhere (no long-press, swipe, or task-detail sheet exists in the source); introduces no fourth hue and no layout restructure; not taste; and the audit's "hit targets 0 failures" is precisely the blind spot, because it measures size, not whether the target is visible.

findings.element: Header facts strip `.headFacts` — "5 of 13 done   1 overdue   day 11 of 97" — against the drawer's "Wedding season · 6 Jul – 10 Oct" and "Day 11 of 97 · 86 days left"
findings.problem: The same fact appears twice in two registers: lowercase "day 11 of 97" in the header, sentence-case "Day 11 of 97" in the drawer. The two strips also use two separator conventions — bare whitespace in the header, middots in the drawer — where the house convention is middots. And the header states an ordinal with no denominator context: 97 of what is answered only inside a drawer the operator may never open. The most actionable number the drawer holds, "86 days left", never reaches the surface the operator lives on.
findings.fix: Nothing to salvage — the dock/scrim reserve is correctly set and no change should be made. If the reviewer's instinct was reaching for something real, it is a different and unrelated observation: `.board` scrolls as a single region, so all five trays scroll in lockstep and a short column (REVIEW, WAITING) cannot be scrolled independently of a long one. That is worth a separate finding on its own merits; it is not this one, and it is not a scrim problem.
findings.why:
REFUTED — the finding is factually wrong on both of its load-bearing claims.

1. Those are not "the last card" of anything. In `data.js` (`window.DENSE_EXTRA`), "Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet" is followed by three more TO DO tasks (Pencil the autumn date / Service the terrace heaters / Replace the two broken chairs); "Walk Aisling & Tom through the orchard on Sunday" is followed by "Repaint the gate posts"; "Gravel delivered for the top car park" is followed by "New signage quote agreed". The tray counts on screen confirm it: TO DO shows 10 with 7 visible, IN PROGRESS 7 with 6, DONE 9 with 8. The frame is the board at scroll top with three-plus cards still below the fold in each column. A gradient fading content that genuinely continues below is the scroll edge doing exactly its job — that is what Linear, Stripe and Vercel all do. The finding has read a mid-scroll fade as a scroll-end erasure.

2. `56px` is not the reserve. `.trayBody { padding: 2px 0 56px }` is not the bottom of the scroll container — the scroll container is `.board`, which carries `padding: 0 16px 96px` with `overflow: auto` (the trays are grid items with auto height; `.trayBody`'s `overflow:auto` never engages because nothing constrains its height, so all five columns scroll together as one region). Clearance below the final card at scroll end is 56 (trayBody) + 4 + 36 (`.trayAdd`) + 8 (`.tray` pad) + 96 (`.board` pad) ≈ 200px, against a 108px scrim. The last card already parks well clear of the gradient. The premise "the reserve was set to the wrong number" inspects the wrong number.

Both halves of the proposed fix would make the artifact worse. `padding-bottom: 132px` stacks on top of the board's existing 96px, giving ~276px of dead white below the final card at scroll end — a visibly broken bottom on every column. Cutting the scrim to 76px is worse still: `.dock` is `bottom: 18px` and 48px tall (5px padding + 38px controls), so its top edge sits 66px off the sheet floor. At 108px the scrim gives ~42px of gradient above the dock, which is why the dock currently reads as floating on a soft edge. At 76px only 10px of gradient sits above the dock top, so fully-inked, fully-legible card text would run straight into the opaque pill with no transition — the exact collision the scrim exists to prevent.

The `pointer-events: none` point is not a defect either: making the scrim capture pointer events would block clicks through its transparent upper 40%, which is strictly worse, and the finding proposes no change there anyway. It is an observation dressed as a fault.

findings.element: `.headFacts` first span, produced by `head()` in floor.html (~line 715: `const done = state === "empty" ? 0 : p.done;`) — visible in locked-dense--1440x960.png
findings.problem: In the dense frame the header states "5 of 32 done" while the DONE tray header states "9", two inches apart on the same screen. `total` is recomputed for the dense set but `done` is hardcoded to the fixture's `p.done = 5`. The same number is also printed twice in two vocabularies on every frame (a fraction in the header, a bare count in the tray), so the operator has two sources for one fact and one of them is wrong. At peak season, the one moment the header stat matters most, it lies.
findings.fix: Discard the re-guttering. The one salvageable grain, if anything is kept: `.trayHead { padding: 0 0 12px }` (drop the `0 4px`), so the column label, pip and count sit on the same left and right lines as the cards in their own column — same region, same column, no rule between them, currently off by 4px. Leave `.head` and `.views` at 20px untouched: they are already flush with each other on both edges, and any change to `.views` padding must be applied asymmetrically or it will break the Share/Planning/… vs Filter/Sort/Display right alignment.
findings.why: Numbers are right, reading is wrong, and the fix regresses. (a) The header pair is already flush: wordmark and the seg TRACK both sit on 120 — the 3px appears only by measuring the inner pill instead of the visible wash track that is the control's object; which of the two owns the line is taste. findings.why: Three of the four premises are factually wrong about what is on screen and in the source, and the fix would break the locked architecture.
