(4) The proposed ink-filled "Add the first task" button inside the tray puts a second heavy primary on the sheet, competing with the dock the locked direction designates as the carrier of add, and duplicating the .trayAdd already in that column. The only true fragment is the punctuation: data.js sets empty: "Nothing held up" with no full stop, and board() line 894 prefers c.empty over EMPTY_COPY.waiting, so the correctly punctuated EMPTY_COPY.waiting ("Nothing held up.") is dead code and the unpunctuated string ships — visible in locked-board--1440x960.png as well as the empty frame. That is a one-character typo, not the finding as stated.

findings.element: `.tag` in `.cardFoot` (floor.html line 396, emitted at line 795) — renders "MARA & FINN", "NORA & CIAN", "VENUE", "ENQUIRY", "BAR" in one identical mono-uppercase slot
findings.problem: Two different taxonomies share one typographic rank: which couple the job belongs to, and which part of the venue does it. A wedding operator's first question is "what is for Saturday's couple" — and on the dense board that answer is carried by the smallest, faintest token on the card, indistinguishable from a department label. Reading down TO DO the operator sees NORA & CIAN, NORA & CIAN, ENQUIRY, AISLING & TOM, VENUE and has to parse each string to know whether it names a client or a work area. The board is organised by status; nothing groups by the event, which is the operator's actual unit of work.
findings.fix: If the panel still wants the couple to lead the scan, the palette-safe and architecture-safe move is not to restyle 30 tags but to prove the grouping the chrome already promises: draw one Display state that groups trays by event rather than status, keeping `.tag` exactly as it is. Failing that, the only legal typographic separation is at ink-3 for both kinds — e.g. area tags keep the 0.1em uppercase mono and client tags lose the uppercase transform — since ink-4 is barred from type by the token contract and ink-2 collides with the adjacent priority token.
findings.why:
REFUTED on four independent grounds, any one of which is fatal.

1. The fix breaks a stated invariant and the measured baseline. `--ink-4: rgba(17,17,17,0.28)` is annotated in floor.html line 44 as "decorative only, never type". Over white that is roughly #b8b8b8, about 2.2:1 — the proposal puts 11px uppercase mono type on it. The audit currently reports 0 WCAG AA contrast failures; this fix would introduce them on the single most-repeated token in the product. `.tag` today is `--ink-3` (5.3:1) and passes.

2. The fix is incoherent against the data model. Every task in data.js carries exactly one `tag` — couple OR area, never both. There is no task anywhere in BOARD or DENSE_EXTRA with two tags, and the card() emitter (floor.html line 795) pushes at most one `.tag` span. So "client always rendered first when both exist" describes a case that does not exist, and `.tag[data-kind="area"] { padding-left: 10px; border-left: 1px solid var(--line-soft) }` would render as an orphan rule floating at the left edge of a lone VENUE / ENQUIRY / BAR token on every area card — a separator separating nothing. Confirmed visually in locked-cards: the AT REST, HOVER, KEYBOARD FOCUS, OVERDUE and DONE specimens all show a single bare tag in the foot.

3. It flattens a rank that already exists. The foot is already a two-step ladder: `.tag` at ink-3 / 400 / mono, and `.hi` (priority) at ink-2 / 600 / sans. Promoting client tags to ink-2 puts "MARA & FINN" at the same ink density as the "High" sitting immediately to its right — two different meanings collapsed onto one colour, with only weight and family left to separate them. On the dense board that is 20+ cards each gaining a darker leading token, raising the board's noise floor against the card title, which is the designed primary read. The fix makes the artifact worse, not better.

4. The premise "nothing groups by the event" is contradicted by what is drawn. Filter, Sort and Display sit in the toolbar top-right of every board frame, and the spine carries project folders. Grouping by couple is exactly what that chrome is for; the finding proposes solving a grouping problem by restyling a label. Additionally, the couple is already carried at title rank on a large share of cards ("Send Nora & Cian three photographer names", "Book the tasting date for Nora & Cian", "Deposit invoice settled, Mara & Finn", "Walk Aisling & Tom through the orchard on Sunday") and in the note line ("Mara & Finn, Saturday").

Minor factual slip: the quoted TO DO reading order is wrong. The dense board's TO DO tags run MARA & FINN, VENUE, ENQUIRY, NORA & CIAN, NORA & CIAN, ENQUIRY, AISLING & TOM, AISLING & TOM, VENUE, VENUE — not the sequence given. Not fatal on its own, but the "indistinguishable" claim also overstates: couple tags are long strings containing an ampersand, area tags are single short words, so the two read apart at a glance even at 11px.

This is a taste preference (one label slot vs two ranks) argued as a defect. One taxonomy-agnostic label rank is standard, deliberate practice at the named bar — Linear puts team, component and type labels in one identical chip rank and lets the string disambiguate.

findings.element: `EMPTY_COPY` and the five `.trayEmpty` blocks in locked-empty--1440x960.png, plus the header on empty
findings.problem: The empty board teaches nothing. Five negations of equal weight sit side by side ("Nothing agreed yet…", "Nothing in motion…", "Nothing waiting on a check.", "Nothing held up", "Nothing finished yet…") — each column already prints a 0, so the words restate the count and then compete with each other for the eye. There is no single starting action, no statement of what the board is for, and no pointer to the dock's Add task. The header still reads "day 11 of 97" over a board with nothing on it, which reads as broken data rather than a fresh start. "Nothing held up" is also the one line missing its full stop.
findings.fix: Three edits, all copy or guard, no structural change. 1. floor.html head() (~line 846): guard the done fact exactly as the overdue and Planning facts are already guarded — `(state === "empty" ? "" : "" + done + " of " + total + " done")`. The empty header then reads "The Orchard, events day 11 of 97". This applies the file's own existing rule to the one fact that was missed; it introduces no new pattern. 2. Kill the duplicate source rather than patching the string. Delete `empty: "Nothing held up"` from the waiting column in data.js:49, and simplify floor.html:894 from `esc(c.id === "waiting" ? c.empty : EMPTY_COPY[c.id])` to `esc(EMPTY_COPY[c.id])`. One string, one place, no future drift. (Patching only data.js leaves both copies alive.) 3. Rewrite EMPTY_COPY (floor.html:873-879) to break the anaphora and avoid restating the tray note above each line: todo: "Add the first thing you have to do." doing: "Move a task across when you start it." review: "Nothing is waiting on a check." waiting: "Nothing is held up." done: "Finished tasks collect here." Read left to right the openings become Add / Move / Nothing is / Nothing is / Finished — the one remaining pair sits on the two genuinely passive columns and reads as deliberate, not as a template. The done line drops "Finished work" so it no longer echoes its own note ("Finished work stays visible."), which the originally proposed "Finished work will collect here." would have preserved. Every line ends in a full stop.
findings.why: Verified in both pixels and code. In locked-empty--1440x960.png the header reads "0 of 0 done", all five tray lines open with "Nothing", and the Waiting line alone lacks a full stop. The strongest evidence is internal inconsistency, not taste: head() (floor.html:838-858) already suppresses two facts on empty — the overdue span and the Planning count <em> both carry a `state === "empty" ? "" :` guard — but leaves the done fact unguarded, so it renders the degenerate "0 of 0 done" while every column already shows its own 0. The file breaks its own rule in one place out of three. The full-stop drift has a root cause the finding did not name: the waiting string is defined twice — EMPTY_COPY.waiting = "Nothing held up." (with stop) at floor.html:879 and data.js:49 empty: "Nothing held up" (without) — and board() at floor.html:894 hard-codes `c.id === "waiting" ? c.empty : EMPTY_COPY[c.id]`, picking the version without the stop. The finding's line cite is wrong (EMPTY_COPY is at 873-879, not 744-750) but every substantive claim holds. Scope is clean: copy plus one render guard, no colour added, no layout restructured, nothing automation could have caught. One correction to the proposed fix — its `done` line "Finished work will collect here." echoes the Done tray note directly above it ("Finished work stays visible."), reproducing a redundancy the current copy already has.

findings.element: Header stack at 390px — `.head`, `.headFacts`, `.views`, `.trayNote` in locked-board--390x844.png
findings.problem: Chrome consumes the top 39% of the phone before a single card appears: wordmark row, then Share/Planning/⋯ row, then title, then facts, then the view segment (which is clipped mid-word at "Calenda"), then the tray name, then the tray description. On the frame a venue operator actually holds while walking the site on a Saturday, one and a half cards are visible. The header is also the least useful part of the screen there — Share and Planning are desk actions.
findings.fix: Keep the copy, derive the number. Leave the chip reading "N days late" — it is the plainest English on the board and the only place magnitude of lateness can be stated — but stop hardcoding it. Change line 785 from `return { kind: "overdue", label: "2 days late" }` to derive from the fixture's own string, matching how lines 786–787 already work: `return { kind: "overdue", label: task.due.replace(/^Overdue by (\d+) days?$/, (_, n) => n + (n === "1" ? " day late" : " days late")) }`. That closes the one real inconsistency (three of four branches derive, one does not), handles the singular case a second overdue task would expose, and changes nothing on screen. Leave the header pill as "1 overdue" — an aggregate count of a class and an instance's specific fact are correctly different registers.
findings.why: Observation is partly accurate (four label shapes do appear; line 785 does hardcode "2 days late"), but the finding fails on four counts. (1) Self-contradictory: it indicts "four grammars" then prescribes four label shapes — "Mon 14 Jul", "Today", "Fri", "1 Aug" — swapping one grammar out and leaving the plurality intact. (2) Unimplementable: grep for `dueDate` and `formatDay` across the entire lab returns zero hits; the fixture carries only strings (`due: "Overdue by 2 days"`), no date primitive, so the prescribed body cannot be written. (3) Factually wrong that "the data model and the chip disagree" — data says "Overdue by 2 days", chip says "2 days late": same state, same number, different register. (4) Misreads the thesis: "severity is expressed by ink density and fill, never by hue" constrains colour, not language; copy already varies by state in every branch ("Today" vs "1 Aug") and must. Worse, the fix degrades the artifact for the stated user — a venue operator gets more from "2 days late" than from "Mon 14 Jul", which demands arithmetic against today at the exact state where speed matters most; the ink fill can say *overdue* but never *how* overdue, so the swap trades away the one fact the loudest object on the board exists to carry. The header/card split ("1 overdue" as aggregate class, "2 days late" as instance fact) is standard Linear/Stripe register, not a defect. Line numbers are also wrong (785, not 656–658). Only genuine residue: the overdue branch is the one branch not derived from data, while lines 786–787 derive from `task.due`/`task.milestone` — a code-hygiene inconsistency in a lab prototype, invisible in every frame since one overdue fixture exists and its literal is correct.

findings.element: .cardTitle (floor.html line 341–345) — every task card title, all trays, all frames
findings.problem: No wrap control at a ~22-character measure, and no line cap. Titles break on function words and strand single-word last lines. In locked-dense: "Waiting on Tom's guest / number before we hold the / room" leaves a four-letter widow alone on line three at 14/600; "Check the spring menu / against the new supplier / list" does the same; "Chase the florist / quote for the / spring date" runs three lines with a violently uneven rag. In locked-cards the LONG TITLE specimen runs three lines under a caption that states "Two lines of title, then the note clamps. A card cannot run away" — the artifact contradicts its own spec. Widows at this frequency are the single most visible type failure across the frames, and they wreck the vertical rhythm of the tray because card heights become arbitrary.
findings.fix: In .cardTitle add: `text-wrap: balance; overflow-wrap: anywhere; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;` and keep `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 62%`. Add `text-wrap: pretty;` to .cardNote (line 347). Balance evens the rag at short measures and kills the one-word last line; the 2-line clamp enforces the stated contract so no card can exceed title-2 + note-2.
findings.why:
Factually wrong about the mechanism, and the fix would make the artifact worse.

(1) Wrong scroller. The finding assumes each tray scrolls and that `.trayBody { padding: 2px 0 56px }` is the entire reserve above the dock. `.board` is the single scroll container — `floor.html`: `.board { flex:1; min-height:0; display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0,1fr)); padding: 0 16px 96px; overflow:auto; }` — which is why `.trayHead` is `position:sticky; top:0` and why all five columns clip at the identical y in locked-dense. Each `.tray` is a grid item stretched to the row height, so `.trayBody`'s own `overflow:auto` never fires.

(2) The reserve is 200px, not 56px. At the end of scroll the last card sits above: trayBody 56 + trayAdd (36 + 4 margin-top) + .tray padding-bottom 8 + .board padding-bottom 96 = 200px. The dock is 48px tall (5 padding + 38 content + 5) at bottom:18px, so a 66px footprint. The last card clears it roughly threefold. The claim "the 56px bottom reserve is smaller than the dock's own 66px footprint" is false.

(3) The named cards are not cut, they are mid-scroll. In locked-dense TO DO reads 10 and shows 7; DONE reads 9 and shows 8. "Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet" and "Gravel delivered for the top car park" fade because three more and one more card sit below them. The scrim is the scroll-edge affordance signalling continuation — the correct behaviour, not hidden work. In locked-board (13 tasks, no overflow) the same full-width scrim is invisible: a white-to-white fade over empty sheet costs nothing.

(4) The fix degrades the work. Padding to 96px adds 40px of dead air at the foot of every column for no gain. Binding the scrim to a centred `min(760px,100%)` radial strips the fade from columns 1 and 5 — the exact two columns the finding names — so their cards would hard-clip mid-word against the sheet's rounded bottom edge, with a visible seam where the radial meets the un-faded columns. A uniform fade across the foot of a full-width scroller is right; a fade covering only the middle ~53% of that scroller is not.

The residual sub-claim (108px scrim for a 66px dock is generous) is taste stated without argument, and the gradient is fully transparent through its first 42% regardless.

findings.element: body { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums } (floor.html line 104) — global, inherited by .cardTitle and .cardNote
findings.problem: Tabular figures are forced into running prose. Every number inside a sentence gets column sidebearings it does not need: "Send midweek rate to the June 2027 walk-in couple", "Ceremony 2pm orchard, drinks terrace, dinner 5:30", "~80 guests, budget-conscious", "Two extra cases of tonic". The 1 in "11", "1 Aug" and "2027" sits in a gaping monospaced slot, so digits inside titles read as a different typeface from the letters around them. Tabular is correct for the counters and chips; it is wrong everywhere text is read as a sentence, and Geist's proportional figures are the whole reason the face looks settled in prose.
findings.fix: Discard the finding as written. There is one small residual defect it brushed past but did not name, worth logging separately at low severity: at 390px the `.word` wordmark wraps onto a row of its own with ~85% of that row empty, because `.head` is `flex-wrap: wrap` (floor.html:717) and `.word` + `.headActions` (search + Share + Planning 5 + ⋯) overflow 390px by a few pixels. That wastes ~32 CSS px and reads as an accident rather than a decision. The minimal correction is to let the ghost labels drop at ≤720px — keep the icons for Share and Planning, keep their tap targets and the Planning count, and the row fits beside the wordmark. That reclaims a row without hiding search, without hiding tray descriptions, and without touching `.seg`.
findings.why:
Refuted on three independent grounds — the impact claim is false, the scroll defect is already handled, and the fix causes a regression.

1) FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT THE FRAME. The finding's headline evidence is "one and a half cards are visible." In locked-board--390x844.png (780x1688 at 2x) the first card top sits at y≈632 and the sheet foot at y≈1530. Three complete cards render above it — "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" (632–893), "Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open day" (905–1093), "Send midweek rate to the June 2027 walk-in couple" (1108–1360) — plus the "+ Add task" affordance at y≈1425 and ~100px of slack before the dock. The proposed fix promises "three cards above the fold"; the artifact already shows three cards and an add affordance. The stated benefit is already delivered, so the 200px it claims to return buys a fourth card, not a first-to-third.

2) THE "39% chrome" NUMBER CONFLATES CHROME WITH COLUMN CONTENT. Header chrome (`.head` through `.views`) ends at y≈490 = 245 CSS px of 844 = 29%, not 39%. The remaining 8% is the tray head ("TO DO 3") and `.trayNote`, which are the column's own content, not header.

3) THE CLIPPED "Calenda" IS ALREADY A SCROLLER. floor.html:723 — `@media (max-width: 720px) { .views { padding: 14px 16px 12px; overflow-x: auto; } }`. Calendar is already reachable; the half-visible item is the standard affordance telling the operator so. The proposed fix also targets the wrong element: `.seg` is the inline-flex pill itself, and giving it `overflow-x: auto` would clip the active item's `box-shadow: var(--ring), var(--raise)` (floor.html:259–262), visibly breaking the lifted Board pill.

4) THE FIX WOULD MAKE IT WORSE. `.headSearch` is a child of `.headActions` (floor.html:851–852), it is `display: none` by default and switched to `inline-flex` only at ≤720px (floor.html:246, 721) — precisely because `.dock, .dockScrim { display: none }` at that breakpoint (floor.html:741). Collapsing `.headActions` to the `⋯` button alone deletes the only search entry point on the phone. On a 32-task peak-season board (locked-dense), search is the operator's primary find mechanism.

5) `.trayNote { display: none }` ON MOBILE FIGHTS A STATED PRODUCT PRIORITY. The compact rule (floor.html:643) proves the descriptions are droppable when the operator chooses compact density — not that they should be dropped by default on the device a venue operator meets the product on. "Agreed and ready to start." / "Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision." is exactly the self-explaining column copy AGENTS.md's utility priority and the first-contact test require. Making the phone the one place a non-PM user gets no explanation inverts it.

6) "Share and Planning are desk actions" is asserted, not argued. Planning carries a live count of 5; on a Saturday walk-round that is the drawer telling the operator what is scheduled. No evidence is offered that either is desk-only.

The finding is a taste preference for a shorter mobile header, stated as a measured defect, with the measurement wrong and the remedy already partly shipped and partly destructive.

findings.element: .word (17px / 600 / -0.045em) beside .headName (18px / 600 / -0.03em), separated by .headRule — the sheet header in every frame
findings.problem: Two 600-weight lockups sit 1px apart in size, which is below the perceptual threshold, so the header reads as two co-equal titles and a 1px rule is left doing all the hierarchy work — nothing states whether "tasks." or "The Orchard, events" is the subject of the page. Worse, the tracking curve inverts at exactly these two elements: the SMALLER item is tracked 50% tighter (-0.045em at 17px vs -0.03em at 18px). Tracking must loosen as size falls; here it does the opposite, and "tasks." reads visibly cramped next to a name set on the same baseline. On the 390px frame the two stack and the failure is total — they are indistinguishable in rank.
findings.fix: No fix warranted; the proposal should be discarded. The only residue worth noting is that both phrases are co-visible in the planning frame ~150 CSS px apart. If that were ever worth addressing, the remedy runs opposite to the proposal — suppress the day-count in .headFacts while the drawer is open, since the drawer states it with the axis bar for context — not import the drawer's punctuation and redundant remainder into the header. That is a separate finding, and a weak one.
findings.why:
The finding's central premise is factually inverted. It claims "the house convention is middots" — but the middot appears exactly twice in the artifact's entire user-facing copy, and both are in the drawer, both inside running prose in a

(data.js:160 "Wedding season · 6 Jul – 10 Oct", data.js:161 "Day 11 of 97 · 86 days left"). The only other · in floor.html is the tag. The artifact's actual inline-fact-strip convention is a flex gap with no separator glyph: .cardFoot { display: flex; gap: 10px } (floor.html:356) renders "MARA & FINN High 💬 1" on every populated card, 13 on the board alone, and .headFacts { display: flex; gap: 14px } (floor.html:198) is the identical treatment. Two consistent rules exist — gap for flex strips of discrete objects, middot for sentences — and the header and drawer each follow the correct one. The proposed middot join would also break the strip: .headFacts's middle child is .late, a filled ink pill (background: var(--ink); color: var(--white), 22px), the black "1 overdue" chip visible in the board frame. Joining with · puts a middot immediately before and after a black pill — punctuation flanking an object rather than separating text runs. "86 days left" in the header is arithmetic redundancy: 97 − 11 = 86. The proposed string prints x and 97−x adjacent. The drawer earns both because they annotate the axis bar directly above them (position on the bar, remaining runway between the 6 Jul / 10 Oct endpoints); the header has no bar. The finding also contradicts itself — it says "replace the third fact" but its fix appends rather than replaces. The casing difference is grammar, not register drift: the drawer summary is a standalone paragraph starting a sentence, the header item is a trailing phrase in an inline strip. Every standalone line in the artifact is sentence-capped ("Agreed and ready to start.", "Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.", "Nothing held up"); every strip phrase is not. One rule, two grammatical positions. The fix's second half does clear damage: lowercasing p.summary leaves a lone lowercase sentence-start sandwiched between the sentence-case "Wedding season · 6 Jul – 10 Oct" above and the sentence-case help text below — a Cap / lower / Cap stack, visible in the planning frame.

findings.element: .hi (floor.html line 398) — the priority token "High" in .cardFoot, sitting immediately right of .tag "MARA & FINN"
findings.problem: The file's own rule at line 290 reads: "Every micro-label in the product is one rule: Geist Mono, 11px, uppercase, +0.1em, weight 400. Tracking carries the hierarchy, so a small label is never bolded to make it matter." `.hi` breaks all four clauses — it inherits .cardFoot's sans at 12px, stays sentence case, and sets weight 600. The result is two incompatible type registers touching on one footer line, and the bolder of the two is the lesser fact. In locked-dense "High" fires in eight cards and creates a bold speckle that the eye catches before the titles do — a straight hierarchy inversion inside the card.
findings.fix: Keep the token short, make it self-describing, and encode it by ink rather than weight so it obeys the card's own stated grammar. 1. floor.html:800 — emit the phrase, not the orphan adjective, and keep it in the foot's own voice (sentence case, Geist sans), so it stays visually distinct from the mono uppercase tag by family and case rather than by weight: `if (task.priority && !done) bits.push('' + esc(task.priority) + ' priority');` renders "High priority", not "HIGH PRIORITY". Do NOT give it .tag's mono/uppercase/0.1em treatment — that merges it with the tag and overflows the 390px foot. 2. floor.html:402 — drop the 600 and express the token by ink density, which is the grammar the specimen caption at line 977 already claims for severity: `.hi { color: var(--ink-1); font-weight: 400; }` ink-1 at 21:1 still reads as the strongest thing in the foot (tag and comment count sit at ink-3, 5.3:1), so priority keeps its rank without borrowing the title's weight. Contrast improves rather than regresses. 3. Guard the foot, since the string gets longer: add `flex-wrap: wrap; row-gap: 4px;` to `.cardFoot` (line 356) so a long tag plus the phrase cannot overflow or collide with the `.grow` note glyph on the 390x844 frame. Re-shoot locked-board--390x844 and locked-dense to confirm no wrap on the longest pairing ("NORA & CIAN" + "High priority" + note glyph). Net effect: the foot reads "MARA & FINN High priority" — one mono label, one plain-English phrase, no orphan adjective, no second bold string competing with the title, and severity carried by ink density exactly as the card's own caption says it is.
findings.why: CONFIRMED, with the fix rewritten. findings.element: `<span class="tick">` inside card() (rendered as `'<span class="tick">' + I.check`), and `.cardDots { opacity: 0 }` revealed only by `.card:hover .cardDots`
findings.problem: The completion control — the single most important verb in a task product, and the one the whole 'Done = filled ink tick' rule is built on — is a bare `<span>`: no button, no role, no tabindex, no accessible name, no activation. It is mouse-only and invisible to assistive tech; a keyboard or screen-reader operator cannot complete a task at all. Compounding it, `.cardDots` (`aria-label="Task actions"`) is a real focusable `<button>` held at `opacity: 0`, revealed only on `:hover`. Opacity applies to the whole subtree including the focus outline, so tabbing to it focuses a control that renders nothing — a focused, invisible button on every card. The card itself is `<article tabindex="0">` with no role and no accessible name, so the tab stop it creates announces only its raw text.
findings.fix: Route every card ring through one custom property so state can never clobber interaction, and cover the theme variants the original fix missed. (a) `.card { --card-ring: var(--ring); box-shadow: var(--card-ring); }`. (b) Convert the state rules to set only the token: `.card[data-done] { background: transparent; --card-ring: 0 0 0 1px var(--line-soft); }` and `.card[data-next] { --card-ring: 0 0 0 1px var(--indigo-line); }`. (c) MOVE the hover/focus/selected/drag rules (L321-328) to sit AFTER the state block (below L410), each setting only `--card-ring`: hover `var(--ring-strong), var(--raise)`; focus `0 0 0 1px var(--indigo), 0 0 0 4px var(--indigo-ring)` keeping `outline: none`; selected `0 0 0 1.5px var(--indigo)`; drag keeps its transform and `--card-ring: var(--lift)`. (d) Do the same for the card registers or the bug survives one toggle away: `[data-cards="flat"] .card:hover` (L600) is still declared before `[data-cards="flat"] .card[data-done]` (L601), and `[data-cards="elevated"]` (L609/610) has the same ordering — convert all of L599-610 and L667 to set `--card-ring` instead of `box-shadow`, with the hover/focus rules ordered last within each block. (e) Fix the tick and menu the same way: `.card[data-done] .tick` (L407) currently kills the hover tick from L342 — give the tick its own `--tick-ring` token and order the hover rule after the done rule. (f) Separately, DELETE the `border-radius: var(--r-chip);` line from `a:focus-visible, button:focus-visible, [tabindex]:focus-visible` (L115) — the outline already follows each element's own border-radius in every current engine, and that one declaration is what collapses `.dockPrimary` and `.segItem` from 999px, `.railTile` from 12px, and `.card` from 12px, all to 6px, on keyboard focus. (g) Finally, add a real focus-visible specimen for a Done card to the spec sheet, since the current `data-force` specimens are what let the automated 5-state audit report zero WCAG failures on a board that has six.
findings.why: Both defects are real in floor.html and invisible to the automated audit. (1) `.card:hover` (L321) and `.card:focus-visible` (L322) are (0,2,0) and declared BEFORE `.card[data-done]` (L405) and `.card[data-next]` (L410), which are also (0,2,0) and redeclare box-shadow — later wins, so the state rules clobber the interaction ring while `outline:none` from L322 survives unopposed. Cards are focusable (`<article class="card" tabindex="0">`, L804). data.js confirms 13 tasks with 5 `lane:"done"` plus 1 `milestone:` = 6 of 13 cards with zero visible keyboard-focus indicator, a WCAG 2.4.7 failure; the board frame matches (5 in DONE, 1 indigo Menu tasting). The specimen sheet asserts "The edge darkens" (L964) and "A real focus ring in the accent" (L965) using `data-force` on t-04/t-08, neither done nor milestone — so the sheet documents behaviour a fifth of the board lacks, which is exactly why the 5-state audit passed. (2) L112-115 sets `border-radius: var(--r-chip)` (6px) on the ELEMENT, not the outline; `button:focus-visible` (0,1,1) and `[tabindex]:focus-visible` (0,2,0) beat the single-class base rules, so on keyboard focus `.dockPrimary` (button, L908) and `.segItem` (a[tabindex], L864) collapse 999px to 6px, `.railTile` (L823) 12px to 6px, and `.card` itself 12px to 6px — pills and card corners deform under the keyboard. Two corrections to the finding: `.dockAvatar` (L910) and `.railAvatar` (L833) are plain non-focusable `<span>`s, so their 50% circles never take the rule; and hover on done/milestone cards is not fully dead — `.cardDots` opacity (L375) is untouched, so the menu still appears, though the edge and tick hover (L342 vs L407) are gone. Neither correction changes the verdict. No constraint is violated: no new hue, no layout change, no type change.

findings.element: .drawer (position:absolute; right/top/bottom: var(--inset); width:388px; background:var(--white); border-radius:var(--r-sheet)) in the planning frame
findings.problem: The drawer is white, on the same inset, with the same 16px radius, with no ring, no shadow and no scrim, sitting directly on top of a white sheet that does not move. The result in locked-planning--1440x960.png is not a panel opening — it is the board being sliced: the WAITING column's description is cut mid-word ('Held by a reply, a delive'), the DONE column and its five cards vanish with no cue they exist, and there is no drawn seam anywhere to explain why. Every other elevation in this file is honestly declared (--ring, --raise, --lift); this one, the largest surface in the product, has none. The dock also stays centred on the full sheet, so it now reads visibly off-centre against the remaining board. Additionally the drawer is an `<aside>` with no accessible name, so nothing announces what opened.
findings.fix:
Dock: the minimal correct repair is one declaration — add `width: max-content` to `.dock`, keeping `left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`. A specified width is not subject to the shrink-to-fit available-space constraint, so the dock sizes to content and the translate re-centres it. If you prefer the symmetric form, `.dock { left: 0; right: 0; margin-inline: auto; width: max-content; max-width: calc(100% - 32px); transform: none; }` is equally correct; the max-width never binds (at 768 it allows ~636px against ~369px needed) and the dock is `display:none` below 720 anyway. `white-space: nowrap` on `.dockField span` / `.dockPrimary span` is redundant once width is max-content — keep it only as belt-and-braces, and be aware it converts any future shrink into overflow rather than wrap.

headFacts: replace the 900px `display: none` with `.headFacts > span:not(.late) { display: none }` so the overdue chip survives 721-900px while the done-count and day-count drop. Verify the empty state at 768 too: `.late` is not emitted there (floor.html:848), so `.headFacts` becomes a zero-width flex box; the stray `.head` gap is absorbed by `.headActions { margin-left: auto }`, so no guard is needed, but confirm it in the shot rather than assuming. Re-capture locked-board--768x1024.png and locked-empty at 768 after the change — the dock and header are the two things the diff must show fixed.
findings.why: Both defects verified in source and pixels. (1) floor.html:431 `.dock { position:absolute; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%) }` with no width — shrink-to-fit resolves against containing-block minus left, i.e. 50% of the sheet. At 768 the sheet is ~667px, capping the dock at ~334px (measured ~343px in locked-board--768x1024.png) against ~369px of content (dockField min-width 196 + dockPrimary ~110 + rule + 34px avatar + gaps + 5px padding). The frame shows 'Search this project' broken over two lines and the primary CTA 'Add task' broken over two lines inside its pill, deforming the pill against the avatar. (2) floor.html:691 hides .headFacts at max-width:900px and line 722 only restores it at max-width:720px, so 721-900px loses the whole facts row. Cross-checked three frames: 1440 shows '5 of 13 done', the filled-ink '1 overdue' chip and 'day 11 of 97'; 390 shows all three on their own row; 768 shows none. The filled ink overdue chip — the loudest object in the design and the anchor of the status language — is present either side of the tablet band and absent inside it. Neither is caught by the passing audit (nothing off-palette, off-weight or under contrast). Markup at line 846 confirms the three facts are span children with .late as the middle one, so the proposed selector is valid against the real DOM. No constraint is violated: no hue introduced, no architecture moved, both are layout-defect repairs inside the locked direction.

findings.element: .dock (position:absolute; left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%)) and @media (max-width: 900px) { .headFacts { display: none } }, both as rendered at 768x1024
findings.problem: Two failures in the same responsive band, both visible in locked-board--768x1024.png. (1) An absolutely positioned element with `left:50%` and no width gets a shrink-to-fit width computed against only the remaining 50% of the containing block. At 768px the sheet is ~668px wide, so the dock is capped at ~334px against ~390px of content: 'Search this project' breaks to two lines and the primary CTA 'Add task' breaks to two lines inside its pill. The product's main call to action is visibly broken on tablet. (2) `.headFacts` is hidden at max-width:900px and only restored at max-width:720px, so between 721px and 900px — precisely the 768 tablet a venue coordinator carries — the '1 overdue' filled ink chip disappears. The loudest object in the entire design, the one the palette rules were written around, is present at 1440 and at 390 and absent at 768.
findings.fix: None worth taking. The only residue with any argument behind it is unrelated to the stated fault: the scrim ramp reaches 0.90 alpha at 42% of its 108px, so mid-scroll text degrades over ~45px rather than gracefully — a softer ramp (0.9 nearer 60%) is arguable. That is a taste call about the fade curve, not the padding, the nested scroller, or the sticky context, all of which measure correct as built. Take no action on this finding.
findings.why:
REFUTED — the structural fault does not exist, and the proposed fix is geometrically a no-op.

Measured in Chromium at 1440x960, state=dense&v=locked (floor.html, live DOM, not inference):

1. "Each tray is a nested scroller inside the board scroller." The declaration exists (`.trayBody { overflow: auto }`, floor.html:304) but it never scrolls. All five trays measure scrollHeight === clientHeight (To do 1123/1123, In progress 859/859, Review 542/542, Waiting 287/287, Done 893/893). The board is already the single scroll surface: `.board` scrollHeight 1333 vs clientHeight 811. The grid row is content-sized to the tallest tray, so no trayBody can ever overflow. Redundant CSS, not a live fault, and it clips nothing.

2. "The sticky .trayHead belongs to the wrong scroll context." False. `.trayHead` is a sibling of `.trayBody`, not a descendant (floor.html:888–896), so its nearest scrollport is `.board`. Verified working: with board.scrollTop = 250, boardTop 130 / headTop 131 — pinned. It is already in the correct and only functioning scroll context.

3. "The 96px board padding never actually protects the inner scroller's content." This is the load-bearing claim and it is empirically false. Scrolled to maxScroll (522), the tallest tray's last card bottom sits at y=741.9 while the scrim starts at y=834 — 92px of clearance, and 137px above the scrim's 0.9-alpha point (879.4). "Add task" lands at 837.9, i.e. 3.9px into the scrim's fully transparent leading edge. Every tray's last card is fully legible with clear air above the dock. The 96px padding is doing exactly its job, tuned to land the Add-task affordance on the scrim's zero-alpha edge. Screenshot of the bottom-scroll state confirms it.

4. "trayAdd is pinned by the inner scroller." False. It flows: To do's trayBody ends at 1319.9, trayAdd top 1323.9 (4px margin). Short trays behave the same — Waiting's body ends 484.1, its Add task at 488.1, sitting directly under the second card, not at the column foot. Visible in locked-dense too.

5. The fix changes nothing. Space below the last card today: 56 (body pb) + 4 + 36 (add) + 8 (tray pb) + 96 (board pb) = 200px, matching the measured 200.1. Proposed: 8 (grid gap) + 36 + 8 + 148 = 200px. Identical resting geometry, identical mid-scroll behaviour, in exchange for a DOM restructure that also moves trayAdd from a 4px-margin flex child into the 8px-gap card grid, coarsening a tuned rhythm.

What the finding actually saw in locked-dense is the intended state: a board scrolled to top, with content passing under a deliberate fade beneath a floating dock — the locked architecture's own mitigation, and the only continuation cue the board has. Reading a scroll-fade as "work disappearing" is a taste assertion dressed as a structural defect; removing or weakening it would leave a hard clip under a floating pill, which is worse.

findings.element: head() in floor.html — `const done = state === "empty" ? 0 : p.done;` — as rendered in locked-dense--1440x960.png
findings.problem: `total` is recomputed for the dense state (13 + DENSE_EXTRA = 32) but `done` is not: it stays at the fixture's `p.done` of 5. The delivered dense frame therefore reads '5 of 32 done' in the header while the DONE tray immediately below it is labelled 9 and renders nine ticked cards. The board contradicts itself by four tasks, in the one state that exists to prove the design survives peak season. The header's own count is also the only number an operator glances at; a board that miscounts its own completions is not shippable at any visual standard. (`1 overdue` is hardcoded the same way — `timeOf` returns the literal string '2 days late' for every overdue task regardless of data, so any second overdue task in a real workspace would claim the same lateness.)
findings.why: Verified in code and pixels. floor.html:477-485 gives .drawer no box-shadow and there is no scrim; .sheet does not move (renderApp line 992 appends the drawer as a sibling). Pixel sampling locked-planning--1440x960.png at the computed drawer edge (1034 CSS / 2068 device px) returns pure #ffffff at y=900/1400/1800 — there is no drawn seam of any kind, white sheet meeting white drawer at zero delta. The concealment is real and consequential: locked-board--1440x960.png shows DONE with 5 cards, the Filter/Sort/Display row, and the headActions cluster (including the Planning button that opened the drawer) all present, and all invisible in the planning frame with no cue. The WAITING note is guillotined mid-word — data.js:48 is "Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.", the frame stops at "delive", and .trayNote (line 303) has no clamp, so this is a clip, not a truncation. The dock is left:50% of the full sheet (line 432) and sits ~260px right of the visible board centre. floor.html:918 emits <aside class="drawer"> with no accessible name. This is in scope: it is a state failure, not a layout redesign, and needs no new colour. The proposed fix is directionally right but wrong in two specifics: the suggested 0 8px 40px rgba(17,17,17,0.10) is exactly the "one soft blur" the file forbids at line 96 and sits off the declared shadow-alpha ladder (2-3-6-8-16); and a bare margin-right would crush trays from ~260px to ~178px at 1440 because .board is repeat(5, minmax(0,1fr)) above 1200px. Confirmed with the fix sharpened.
